headline: Highest risk is medium: shared API/network surfaces create plausible prompt, leakage, and workflow-conflict paths, but no direct shared workspace or documented interaction is provided.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: PaddleOCR can run browsers and call APIs, while Superset calls the Superset API and also has network egress. No shared channel or direct ingestion path is documented, so prompt injection is only plausible through unusual copy/paste or external bridging, not default interaction.
conditions: IF an operator copies PaddleOCR output into Superset inputs without sanitization, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared clipboard or message queue, attacker-controlled text can bridge them.
mitigations: Disable copy/paste bridging between outputs and inputs.
Sanitize OCR text before any downstream use.
Require provenance labels on imported text.
Use separate operator sessions for each agent.

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images and has allowlisted egress; Superset touches no declared sensitive classes and also has allowlisted egress. The profiles do not show a shared workspace or secrets, so leakage is possible only if the operator places sensitive files into both tools or exports OCR content into Superset.
conditions: IF the same sensitive document set is loaded into both agents, both can expose it through their outputs or API calls.
IF Superset is configured to ingest OCR-derived text, document contents can propagate beyond the original workflow.
mitigations: Keep sensitive documents out of shared folders.
Restrict both agents to separate workspaces.
Review outbound API destinations before processing.
Redact sensitive fields before OCR export.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: PaddleOCR has browser and API-call capability, while Superset has API-call capability. No filesystem write, git, or database write permissions are shown for either agent, so direct write-write conflict is not evidenced; only limited overlap on external API use exists.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external API resource, they may overwrite each other's state.
IF an orchestrator grants hidden write permissions not shown in the profiles, conflict severity increases.
mitigations: Assign distinct API credentials per agent.
Add request serialization at the orchestrator.
Audit for hidden write scopes before deployment.

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR produces document-derived text, and Superset can consume API-driven analytics workflows. If Superset treats OCR output as authoritative without verification, transcription errors can cascade into dashboards or decisions. The profiles do not show explicit validation gates, so the interaction is inferred and should be treated conservatively.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is imported into Superset dashboards without human review, OCR mistakes can propagate.
IF Superset automates actions from imported text, downstream errors become operational.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before import.
Compare OCR output against source documents for critical fields.
Mark OCR-derived fields as untrusted metadata.
Disable automated actions on imported text.

E_compliance.rationale: PaddleOCR is documented as touching documents and images, but neither profile shows regulated data classes, residency constraints, or retention differences. Superset likewise shows no compliance-specific handling. With no documented mismatch, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are introduced into either agent, a separate compliance review is required.
IF future configuration adds residency or retention differences, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Document the data classes before deployment.
Confirm retention settings for any regulated data.
Keep regulated data out of both agents unless reviewed.
